text: BENDING 6.4.1 Field Bends Cold bends are to be field fabricated in accordance with the provisions outlined in 49 CFR, Part 195, ASME B31.4, and Project Specification. Cold bends will not be bent more than 1.5 degrees per pipe diameter as measured along the pipe axis. All field bends (or PIs) over the selected maximum deflection angle of 30 degrees will be assumed as an induction bend or segmentable fitting. 6.4.2 Induction Bends Induction bends shall be consistent with ASME B16.49 ‐ Factory–Made Wrought Steel Buttwelding Induction Bends for Transportation and Distribution Systems. Induction bends shall have a minimum bend radius of five (5) pipe diameters (5D) with two (2) foot tangents on each side of the bend. Segmentable fittings shall have a minimum bend radius of three (3) pipe diameters (3D) with two (2) foot tangents on each end. 6.5 WELDING All welding of the mainline, and associated Launchers, Receivers, and mainline valve station piping will be in accordance with API‐1104 and Project Specifications. 6.6 NON‐DESTRUCTIVE EXAMINATION (NDE) During construction, 100% of the field welds will be inspected. The preferred methods of NDE (i.e., ultrasonic, x‐ray, etc.) for the different types of welds will be evaluated and selected during the Detailed Design phase of the project. 6.7 CROSSINGS 6.7.1 HDD HDD crossing design and installation requirements shall be in accordance with: Page 13 of 20 Design Basis Memorandum 1997-000-PL-DBM-0001 Revision: 0 Pipeline Scope - FEED Date: April 28, 2023 • NASTT’s Horizontal Directional Drilling (HDD) Good Practices Guidelines – 4th Edition, 2017 • Depth of Cover: Minimum 25 feet under surface obstacles or as required by the site-specific permit or agreement • Entry Angle: 10° to 16° • Exit Angle: 6° to 12° • Bending Radius: R = 100 feet x Pipe Diameter (in inches) • Minimum Horizontal Separation: 25 feet from underground structures and facilities 6.7.2 Water Bodies & Wetlands Special construction procedures for working in water bodies and wetlands will be required to minimize potential damage to these fragile ecosystem areas. Where open trench construction is used, exterior weights may be used to provide negative buoyancy. Water crossings are installed at a depth in order to provide the minimum depths of cover of 4 feet at the lowest point of the stream or pond bed. Greater installation depth may be specified within the crossing permit. 6.7.3 Highways & Roads Road or highway crossings will be designed and installed per state and county permitting requirements. At road crossings, heavier wall pipe will be installed within the road easement limits and will run to the property line or to the extreme edge of the road right‐of‐way.
